title: Local SEO strategy: the ranking factors and five tactics for winning the local pack
summary: A practical guide to local SEO built around Google's three local signals (relevance, prominence, distance). It covers key ranking factors (NAP consistency, localized content, local backlinks, schema) and five tactics: Google Business Profile, citations, website optimization, content, and customer reviews.

principles.text: Local rankings come down to three signals: relevance, prominence, and distance. You can't change distance, so win on the other two.
principles.quote: Although it’s impossible to change your physical distance from the searcher, a great local SEO strategy can assist your company in matching Google’s other ranking criteria

principles.text: Keep NAP (name, address, phone) identical everywhere; inconsistency makes search engines doubt you're legitimate.
principles.quote: All local businesses should observe this since an inconsistent NAP can confuse search engines, which could lead them to think you are not legitimate or have multiple businesses.

principles.text: Claim and fully fill out your Google Business Profile first; it's the cheapest, highest-leverage local move.
principles.quote: A Google My Business (GMB) page should be at the top of every business’s local SEO to-do list because it is the simplest approach to promoting brand awareness.

principles.text: Audit your citations by searching your NAP, misspellings and wrong addresses to find inconsistent or duplicate listings, then fix them.
principles.quote: You can also use methods like misspelling your brand name, typing a slightly different address than the real location, or finding duplicate listings to help figure out your inconsistent citations online.

principles.text: Reviews are a top-three local pack factor; ask for them through many channels and respond to every one.
principles.quote: To get into the local pack, you’ll need customer reviews, which are one of the top three ranking variables.

principles.text: Write content about your whole industry and area, not just sales pitches, to position yourself as the local authority.
principles.quote: Instead of looking for ways to sell your products and services, when writing content, choose a topic that represents your business as a whole.
